name: North Coast

contains: Green Valley of the Russian River Valley
Oak Knoll District of Napa Valley

climate: Seasons this mild ripen Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon, Riesling, Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon fully without cooking off their freshness.
Chardonnay and Cabernet Sauvignon sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Zinfandel is at its cool limit. In cool years it can stay underripe, with green, sharp flavors.
Pinot Noir is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Most rain falls in winter. Dry summers keep mildew and rot down, though young vines may need watering.

soil.rock: Sandstone is sand bound into rock. It weathers to light, sandy soil that drains freely.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: The high ground runs about 7°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.

winkler: Early and mid-season grapes make good wine.

sheet.place: A huge AVA of six counties north of San Francisco, with Napa and Sonoma inside it.

claims.claim: The North Coast AVA was established in 1983.
It covers six counties north of San Francisco: Lake, Marin, Mendocino, Napa, Solano and Sonoma.
It is a very large AVA, over 3 million acres or about 4,700 square miles.
The climate is maritime, shaped by fog and breezes from the Pacific. It spans a wide range of climate regions, from I to IV.
It contains many smaller AVAs, including Napa Valley, Alexander Valley, Russian River Valley, Anderson Valley and Dry Creek Valley.
The name North Coast first meant three counties: Napa, Sonoma and Mendocino. Lake, Marin and Solano were added during the 1980s approval.
Many grapes grow here, including Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Merlot, Zinfandel and Sauvignon Blanc.
A North Coast label lets a winery blend fruit from several counties and sub-AVAs.
